answer: The fix is in django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py, in _WKBReader.read() (the base class of WKBReader). The str branch passed the raw Python str to the C function wkb_reader_read_hex, which needs bytes, so string input crashed. The fix encodes the string first (wkb.encode()) and passes the encoded bytes and their length.

django/db/models/functions/datetime.py (Now.as_oracle): on Oracle, Now() rendered as CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (a TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE), whose type mismatched the plain timestamp values in a bulk_create() insert and made the query crash; the fix renders it as LOCALTIMESTAMP instead. (Identified from the current code and recollection; the ticket text isn't in the corpus.)

The fix changed django/db/backends/base/schema.py (the `_related_non_m2m_objects` helper). What was wrong: when a primary key's type was altered, the schema editor only found the foreign keys that point directly at that field. It missed the foreign keys (e.g. a multi-table-inheritance child's parent_link) that point at the fields which reference it. Those columns kept their old type and their FK constraints weren't dropped and recreated, so the migration crashed. The helper now recurses through the related fields' `remote_field` to cover them. This is from reading the current code, which has that recursion. I couldn't see the ticket or commit in the repo, so I haven't confirmed that this recursion is the change that fixed #33462.

The fix changed django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py, and it also deleted the django/contrib/sitemaps/management/commands/ping_google.py command. `ping_google()` is gone from this module in the checked-out code, so this answer comes from the code state and from my memory of the ticket. I couldn't read the ticket or the diff. What was wrong: `ping_google()` and the `ping_google` command sent requests to Google's sitemap "ping" endpoint, and Google deprecated and then shut that endpoint down. The helper therefore no longer worked, so Django removed it.

The fix changed django/db/models/constraints.py. Before it, BaseConstraint.deconstruct() left a custom violation_error_message out of the kwargs, and the constraint subclasses' __eq__ methods ignored it. As a result, constraints that differed only in that message compared equal, and clone() and migrations lost the message. In the current code, deconstruct() emits violation_error_message when it differs from the default (lines 79-83), and CheckConstraint.__eq__ and UniqueConstraint.__eq__ compare it (lines 160 and 357). I only read the already-fixed code in this corpus, so this is inferred from that code. I did not look at the ticket or the fix commit.

The fix changed django/db/models/sql/compiler.py, in SQLCompiler.get_combinator_sql(). What was wrong: when a sliced union dropped its empty parts, it could be left with a single part that was itself sliced. That produced invalid SQL and a crash. The fix sets `compiler.elide_empty = False` on every part of a sliced union, so empty parts are no longer elided. I found the code by reading the repo, not the ticket text, so I inferred the cause from the fix's code comment.

The title "Hardened binary lookup in template commands" doesn't match the real ticket. Django #33986 is "Code formatters should be looked up before template rendering in startapp/startproject." The fix is in django/core/management/templates.py, which now calls find_formatters() before it renders the templates. It also touched django/core/management/utils.py, which gained find_formatters() and a black_path parameter on run_formatters(). What was wrong: startapp/startproject looked up the external formatter (black) via PATH only after the project files were rendered. Because the lookup came late, it could pick up a "black" that the generated files had put on the path, so the lookup now happens first.

The fix changed django/http/response.py (HttpResponseBase). Pickling an HttpResponse failed because its __dict__ held unpicklable handler state: `_resource_closers` (bound `close` methods, e.g. request.close) and `_handler_class`. The fix added a `__getstate__` that dropped those attributes. This was later reverted (ticket #34482, commit 173034b0), so the corpus doesn't contain the fix. The line given is where `_resource_closers` is set in HttpResponseBase.__init__. I took the fix's content from memory and the revert ticket; I didn't read the original diff.

The fix is in django/db/models/expressions.py. Before it, the `_connector_combinations` table used to infer `CombinedExpression.output_field` had no `Combinable.MOD` entry for mixed numeric operand types (Integer with Decimal, Integer with Float). Combining those with `%` therefore raised a FieldError about mixed types instead of resolving an output_field. The tree I searched already contains the fix, and `Combinable.MOD` is now in the different-type numeric list at line 545. I couldn't look up the ticket text itself, so this comes from the code.

File: django/core/management/commands/inspectdb.py. The generated models had clashing reverse accessors when several fields pointed at the same related table (or when a related_name was missing/non-unique); the fix makes inspectdb generate a unique related_name of the form "<model>_<field>_set" for repeated relations. (Inferred from the current code; I could not view the ticket or diff.)

The fix changed django/db/backends/base/schema.py (BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.table_sql). ExclusionConstraint.constraint_sql() returns a Statement object, not a str. table_sql() passed those values straight to ", ".join(...), so creating a model with an ExclusionConstraint crashed with a TypeError. The fix wraps each item in str(...) before joining. I confirmed the symptom from the ticket text and the fixed code in the repo. I did not see the commit diff itself.

django/core/handlers/asgi.py — ASGIRequest ignored the FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME setting (it only used the ASGI scope's root_path), so script_name/path/path_info were wrong; the fix adds get_script_prefix(scope), which returns settings.FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME when set.

The fix changed django/db/backends/base/schema.py. The problem: _all_related_fields() returned the model's reverse relations in whatever order _meta._get_fields() produced, which isn't deterministic. _related_non_m2m_objects() zips the old and new models' relations by position, so it could pair the wrong old and new relations. The fix sorts the fields by name (sorted(..., key=operator.attrgetter("name"))). I found this in the code only; I couldn't see the ticket text itself, so the description of the bug is inferred from the code and the fix.

The fix is in django/forms/formsets.py (BaseFormSet). What was wrong: the "too many forms" and "too few forms" messages were hard-coded inside full_clean(), so a formset couldn't customize them. The fix adds them to default_error_messages (keys too_many_forms and too_few_forms). It also adds an error_messages argument to __init__, and full_clean() now raises ValidationError using self.error_messages[...]. This is based on the already-fixed code in the corpus. I didn't see the ticket text or the pre-fix code, so the description of the original problem is inferred from the ticket title and the current code.

The fix changed django/core/files/move.py (file_move_safe()). The problem was that, when copying across filesystems, the copystat() call raised PermissionError on SELinux-enabled systems, and the code didn't handle it. The fix catches that error, falls back to copymode(), and ignores a PermissionError from that too, so the move no longer crashes.

django/db/models/fields/__init__.py (CharField.__init__). Value._resolve_output_field returns a bare CharField() for strings, which has max_length=None. CharField.__init__ used to append MaxLengthValidator(self.max_length) unconditionally, so it built a useless MaxLengthValidator(None). That validator would also fail with a TypeError if it ever ran. The fix adds the guard `if self.max_length is not None:` before appending the validator. The CharField.description property has the same check. I did not find the ticket text or the fix commit in the corpus. This is from reading the post-fix code, and it matches my memory of the upstream fix.

django/views/debug.py — the technical 500 debug page only showed the whole source line for each traceback frame and gave no fine-grained location of the failing expression (Python 3.11+ column info from co_positions()); the fix computes start/end columns and passes a ^^^^ underline (colno / tb_area_colno) to the templates.

The fix is in django/db/models/expressions.py, in ResolvedOuterRef.resolve_expression. Before the fix, a subquery that referenced an outer query's window expression through OuterRef wasn't rejected. It produced invalid or broken SQL, because window functions can't be referenced from a subquery. The method now checks `col.contains_over_clause` and raises NotSupportedError ("Referencing outer query window expression is not supported").

The fix changed django/db/models/expressions.py. Exists (a Subquery subclass) inherited empty_result_set_value = None, so Exists() on an empty queryset returned None instead of False. The fix gives Exists its own empty_result_set_value = False. I couldn't open the ticket itself, because the corpus has no ticket text. This comes from reading the current code, not from the commit diff.

File: django/contrib/gis/forms/widgets.py (BaseGeometryWidget). Problem: map size was hard-coded via the map_width/map_height Python attributes (600x400, copied into widget attrs) instead of being styled with CSS; the fix deprecates them, with __init__ emitting a RemovedInDjango51Warning when they're passed in attrs or overridden. This is inferred from the current code; I couldn't read the ticket or commit text.

The fix changed django/db/models/sql/compiler.py (SQLInsertCompiler.as_sql). Before the fix, the ON CONFLICT / ON DUPLICATE KEY clause was built from the field names of unique_fields and update_fields, so fields with a custom db_column produced SQL that used the wrong column name. It now passes each field's db column (f.column) instead. I read the current code in this repo, which already has the fix. I didn't see the original diff, and I'm recalling that the old code used names rather than columns.

django/contrib/auth/forms.py — UserCreationForm/BaseUserCreationForm.__init__ unconditionally accessed self.fields[USERNAME_FIELD] to set autofocus, raising KeyError for subclasses/custom user models whose form omitted that field; the fix guards it with `if USERNAME_FIELD in self.fields`. (Inferred from the code; ticket text not in the repo.)

django/db/backends/postgresql/schema.py — (best inference from the code; the ticket isn't in the corpus) PostgreSQL's schema editor updated rows / altered the table while deferred constraint checks were still pending, so it needed to run SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE alongside the UPDATE (sql_update_with_default) so the data change and following ALTER TABLE could happen in the same transaction.

The fix is in django/db/models/sql/query.py, in Query.build_filter(). Before the fix, build_filter() checked whether the final field was a relation and raised FieldError ("Related Field got invalid lookup: ...") whenever the lookups had more than one part. That check rejected transforms chained on a relation field, such as fk__transform=value. The fix removed the check, so a relation field's column is now built and passed straight to build_lookup(), which applies the transforms. I didn't find the ticket text or the fix commit in this corpus. I inferred the pre-fix behaviour from memory of older Django versions. In the code here, the check is gone and the relation branch is at lines 1489-1499.

The fix changed django/db/models/base.py, in Model._get_field_value_map(). The method wrapped each field value in a bare Value(...) with no output field, so range values such as NumericRange had no resolvable type and CheckConstraint.validate() broke. It now passes the model field, as Value(getattr(self, field.attname), field). I'm recalling the original diff from memory, since the corpus has no ticket or commit text. The current code does match that fix.

The fix is in django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py (it added `_filter_prefetch_queryset`). The ticket's bug was that `prefetch_related()` with a sliced queryset, e.g. `Prefetch('children', Child.objects.all()[:3])`, could not work. The prefetch filtered all related instances with one `__in` query, so a plain LIMIT/OFFSET applied to the whole result instead of to each parent's related objects, and Django refused it. The fix clears the slice and filters on a per-parent `RowNumber()` window function (`partition_by` the relation field) using the slice's low and high marks. It raises NotSupportedError on backends without window-function support.

File: django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py (ContentTypeManager.get_for_models). The DB lookup matched app labels and model names independently, so a stale content type could match because another app had a model with the same name, and the following get_model() call on that stale row crashed. The fix builds one Q(app_label=..., model__in=...) per app label, ORed together.

The fix changed django/contrib/admin/options.py (BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_foreignkey). Previously, for fields in radio_fields it always set kwargs["empty_label"] to _("None") (or None if the field isn't blank), overwriting any empty_label passed in by a subclass; now it uses kwargs.get("empty_label", _("None")), so an overridden empty_label is respected.

django/db/models/sql/query.py (Query.get_aggregation): aggregate() over an aggregate that referenced a Subquery annotation was not wrapped in an inner subquery query, causing a crash; the fix tracks `refs_subquery` (annotations referenced by the aggregate with subquery=True) and forces the subquery-wrapping path when it's set.

The fix is in django/db/models/lookups.py, in the base Lookup class that IsNull inherits from. I could not find the ticket or commit text in the corpus, so this comes from the code and not the ticket. The likely problem: a lookup used directly as a filter expression, such as IsNull(F("x"), True), has a plain bool as its right-hand side, which isn't an expression. Lookup.get_source_expressions() and set_source_expressions() assumed both sides were expressions, so resolving or copying the lookup crashed. They now return and accept only the lhs when the rhs is a direct value.
django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py — the `_WKBReader.read()` method, which handles str input by encoding it to bytes before calling `wkb_reader_read_hex`.

django/db/backends/base/schema.py — the fix is the recursive `yield from _related_non_m2m_objects(old_rel.remote_field, new_rel.remote_field)` in `_related_non_m2m_objects()`. I recall 3.2 returning a plain `zip(...)` with no recursion, so the recursion looks like the fix, but I'm not certain.

corpus/django/contrib/postgres/fields/ranges.py. I'm inferring this from the code and from memory of the upstream commit, not from a changelog or ticket reference.
